To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bilateral intraamygdaloid infusion of the selective GABAAρ receptor antagonist (1,2.5,6-tetrhydropyridin-4-yl) methylphosphinic acid (CGP36742) reduced the exploration of the elevated plus maze without affecting locomotion, and increased the plasma level of corticosterone.

the bilateral intraamygdaloid infusion of the GABARρ antagonist (1,2.5,6-tetrathydropyridine4yl)methylphosinic acid (CGP 36742), but not the GABARαβ antagonist bicuculline, dose-dependently reduces the exploration of the elevated plusmaze without affecting locomotion, and increases the plasma levels of cortisol.

the GABAA ϕ receptor antagonist, (1,2,5,6 -Tetrahydropyrindine-4- yl) methyphosphinic acid (TPMPA), reduced the exploration of the elevated plus maze, an animal model of anxiety, without affecting locomotion or inducing seizures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the GABAR ρ receptor mechanisms of the amygdala and their putative role in anxiety and stress-related behaviors.
the study of the mechanisms of action of the GABAR ρ receptors within amygdala and their role in the modulation the anxiety and fear.
the role of GABAA receptors in fear and anxiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GABAA receptors in the amygdala have anxiolytic and anti-convulsant effects, while GABAA ϱ receptors may have an anxiogenic and convulsant role in the amygadaloid modulation of fear, anxiety and seizures.
the GABAA ϕ receptor is involved in the modulation of anxiety and fear.
GABAA receptors are involved in the modulation of anxiety, and that this effect is mediated by the GABAA ϕ subunit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GABAA receptors, particularly GABAA ρn subunits, are involved in the amygdala in the control of anxiety.
GABAA receptors may be divided into two subtypes: GABAA ϕ and GABAA ϵ.
the activation of GABAA receptors in the amygdala, but not GABAA ρm, is involved in the regulation of anxiety.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GABAA receptor subtypes may have a role as targets for anxiolytics.
GABAA receptors may be an attractive pharmacological target for treating anxiety-related disorders.
the GABAA ϕ receptor may have a role on the amygdaloidal modulation of fear and/or anxiety.
